name: Schwendau
kurzbeschreibung: Village community above Mayrhofen with direct access to the Penken ski area and the Schlegeis reservoir.
text:
Overview

Schwendau lies at 620 meters above sea level in the upper Zillertal valley, nestled in the district of Schwaz directly adjacent to Mayrhofen, Hippach, and Ramsau im Zillertal. Home to approximately 1,800 residents, the municipality stretches across the wide, sunny valley floor west of the Ziller river up to the alpine slopes of Mount Penken and Mount Horberg, reaching altitudes of 2,590 meters. Schwendau comprises the villages of Dorf, Burgstall, Kohlstatt, and Linden. As host to the valley station of the Horbergbahn gondola, Schwendau serves as a central gateway to the vast Mountopolis and Ski Zillertal 3000 ski domains. Despite being right next to Mayrhofen, Schwendau has maintained its quiet, rural charm, featuring traditional farmhouses, alpine hospitality, and diverse four-season recreation.

History

The settlement was first recorded around 1200 as Swentowe in the land register of the Archbishopric of Salzburg. The name derives from Middle High German words denoting cleared land and riverside meadows. In medieval times, Schwendau held significant administrative importance: the Ziller river marked the border between the County of Tyrol and Salzburg. Under the historic Three Linden trees in the hamlet of Linden, the Salzburg bailiff court held judicial assemblies for centuries. In the center of the valley rises the Burgstallschrofen, a glacier-polished rocky knoll where a medieval fortress once stood. In 1845, the neo-Baroque Burgschrofen Chapel was consecrated on this rocky summit to reaffirm Catholic faith following regional religious tensions, connected today by a serene Stations of the Cross path.

Getting there

Schwendau enjoys straightforward access through the Zillertal valley. By car, exit the A12 Inntal motorway at Wiesing/Zillertal and follow federal road B169 south for roughly 28 kilometers towards Mayrhofen, where signs direct motorists to Schwendau and the extensive Horbergbahn parking facilities. Rail travelers alight at Jenbach station to transfer onto the scenic Zillertalbahn narrow-gauge railway, getting off at Bichl stop or Ramsau-Hippach station, just a short walk across the river bridge. Regular regional and ski buses provide seamless connections between Schwendau, Mayrhofen, and the mountain lifts.

Tips

Take the Horbergbahn gondola directly into the Penken ski area, accessing 142 kilometers of groomed slopes, the celebrated PenkenPark freestyle terrain, and Austria's steepest groomed run, the 78% gradient Harakiri. During summer, hike up through shaded forest along the Stations of the Cross to the hilltop Burgschrofen Chapel for rewarding panoramic views. Rock climbers can tackle more than 50 routes on the Burgstallschrofen granite crag, while aviation fans can watch paragliders touch down at the Burgstall landing field or embark on a tandem flight. The level Ziller river promenade offers relaxing walking and cycling paths.
